PROSECUTION HISTORY EXCERPT
United States Patent Application No. 16/234,891
Applicant: Williams IP Holdings, LLC
Date of Remarks: April 2, 2019
Examiner: James R. Whitfield, Art Unit 3686
Title: System and Method for Dynamic Network Optimization

APPLICANT'S REMARKS IN RESPONSE TO OFFICE ACTION DATED JANUARY 15, 2019

[Bates: WILL-PH-000231]

... [pages 1-3 omitted] ...

III. REMARKS REGARDING THE § 101 AND § 112 REJECTIONS

A. Response to § 101 Rejection (Claims 1-8)

The Examiner rejected Claims 1-8 under 35 U.S.C. § 101 as being directed
to an abstract idea. The rejected claims include the limitations
"dynamically reconfiguring" network parameters, the "optimization module" for
performing algorithmic computations, and the "interconnect module" for
routing data between system components.

[Bates: WILL-PH-000232]

Applicant acknowledges that the asserted method claims may be directed to
an abstract idea under the Alice step-one framework and that the
means-plus-function limitations lack corresponding structural disclosure
sufficient to avoid indefiniteness under 35 U.S.C. 112(b). Applicant
respectfully submits, however, that the claims as a whole, including the
specific "dynamically reconfiguring" step and the "optimization module"
and "interconnect module" elements, amount to significantly more than the
abstract idea by providing a concrete technical improvement to network
optimization systems, thereby satisfying Alice step two.

B. Response to § 112 Rejection (Claims 3, 5, 7)

The Examiner also rejected Claims 3, 5, and 7 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) for
indefiniteness, specifically as to the "optimization module" and
"interconnect module" limitations. Applicant contends that the specification
at paragraphs [0045]-[0062] and [0078]-[0091] provides sufficient algorithmic
disclosure to satisfy the structural requirements under Aristocrat Technologies
Australia Pty Ltd. v. International Game Technology, 521 F.3d 1328 (Fed.
Cir. 2008), and WMS Gaming Inc. v. International Game Technology, 184 F.3d
1339 (Fed. Cir. 1999).

[Bates: WILL-PH-000233]

Applicant therefore requests that the Examiner reconsider the § 101 and
§ 112 rejections in view of the foregoing remarks and the amendments
submitted herewith.

Respectfully submitted,
/John M. Patterson/
Registration No. 52,441
Patterson & Associates Patent Law
April 2, 2019

[END OF EXCERPT]

JOINT CLAIM CONSTRUCTION AND PREHEARING STATEMENT
Williams IP Holdings, LLC v. PatentCo Holdings, Inc.
Case No. 2024-CV-0493 (Judge Sandra Okafor)
Pursuant to Patent Local Rule 4-3
Filed: October 28, 2024

=================================================================
I. DISPUTED CLAIM TERMS
=================================================================

The parties have identified the following disputed claim terms, phrases,
or clauses from U.S. Patent No. 10,412,887 (the "'887 Patent"):

-----------------------------------------------------------------
DISPUTED TERM 1: "dynamically reconfiguring"
(Claims 1, 4, 8)
-----------------------------------------------------------------

Plaintiff Williams IP Proposed Construction:
  "Automatically adjusting network parameters in real time in response to
  detected changes in network conditions, without requiring manual
  intervention"

Defendant PatentCo Holdings Proposed Construction:
  "Reprogramming hardware components during operation"

Intrinsic Evidence Cited by Plaintiff:
  - '887 Patent, col. 4:12-28; col. 7:3-19
  - Prosecution History: Applicant Remarks dated April 2, 2019
    (WILL-PH-000231-233): Applicant stated that the "dynamically
    reconfiguring" step provides a concrete technical improvement to
    network optimization systems. See also applicant's acknowledgment at
    WILL-PH-000232 that "the asserted method claims may be directed to an
    abstract idea under the Alice step-one framework and that the
    means-plus-function limitations lack corresponding structural disclosure
    sufficient to avoid indefiniteness under 35 U.S.C. 112(b),"
    which the applicant sought to overcome via Alice step two.

Intrinsic Evidence Cited by Defendant:
  - '887 Patent, col. 2:45-67 (describing hardware reconfiguration)
  - Prosecution History: Same April 2, 2019 remarks (WILL-PH-000232)

-----------------------------------------------------------------
DISPUTED TERM 2: "optimization module"
(Claims 3, 5, 7)
-----------------------------------------------------------------

Plaintiff Williams IP Proposed Construction:
  "A software component that performs computations to identify and apply
  optimal network configuration parameters based on current conditions"

Defendant PatentCo Holdings Proposed Construction:
  Governed by 35 U.S.C. § 112(f) as means-plus-function; corresponding
  structure: none adequately disclosed; claim indefinite.

Intrinsic Evidence Cited by Plaintiff:
  - '887 Patent, col. 8:14-52; col. 9:3-31; paragraphs [0045]-[0062]
  - Prosecution History: April 2, 2019 Applicant Remarks (WILL-PH-000232):
    Applicant acknowledged that the asserted method claims may be directed
    to an abstract idea under the Alice step-one framework and that the
    means-plus-function limitations lack corresponding structural disclosure
    sufficient to avoid indefiniteness under 35 U.S.C. 112(b), while
    arguing the specification at paragraphs [0045]-[0062] provides
    sufficient algorithmic structure under Aristocrat Technologies.

Intrinsic Evidence Cited by Defendant:
  - '887 Patent, col. 8:14-52 (asserting insufficient structural disclosure)
  - Prosecution History: WILL-PH-000232 (applicant's own acknowledgment of
    structural disclosure deficiency)

-----------------------------------------------------------------
DISPUTED TERM 3: "interconnect module"
(Claims 5, 7, 9)
-----------------------------------------------------------------

Plaintiff Williams IP Proposed Construction:
  "A hardware or software component that manages data routing between the
  optimization module and external network interfaces"

Defendant PatentCo Holdings Proposed Construction:
  Governed by 35 U.S.C. § 112(f) as means-plus-function; corresponding
  structure: none adequately disclosed; claim indefinite.

Intrinsic Evidence Cited by Plaintiff:
  - '887 Patent, col. 10:7-44; col. 11:2-19; paragraphs [0078]-[0091]
  - Prosecution History: April 2, 2019 Applicant Remarks (WILL-PH-000232):
    Same acknowledgment regarding abstract idea and structural disclosure
    applies to "interconnect module" as a means-plus-function limitation.
    Applicant cited paragraphs [0078]-[0091] as providing sufficient
    algorithmic structure.

Intrinsic Evidence Cited by Defendant:
  - '887 Patent, col. 10:7-44 (asserting insufficient structural disclosure)
  - Prosecution History: WILL-PH-000232 (same applicant acknowledgment)

=================================================================
II. AGREED CONSTRUCTIONS
=================================================================

The parties agree to the following constructions:

Term: "network parameters"
Agreed Construction: "Configurable settings that govern the behavior of
network components, including routing tables, bandwidth allocation, and
quality-of-service settings"

Term: "real-time"
Agreed Construction: "Without perceptible delay relative to the triggering
event"

=================================================================
Document prepared by counsel for both parties.
Last revised: October 28, 2024.

CLAIM CONSTRUCTION BRIEF: WILLIAMS IP v. PATENTCO HOLDINGS, 2024-CV-0493

[DRAFT v1 - For Review and Finalization]
[Matter M-2024-006]

IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE [DISTRICT]

WILLIAMS IP HOLDINGS, LLC,
    Plaintiff,

v.

PATENTCO HOLDINGS, INC.,
    Defendant.

Case No. 2024-CV-0493
Judge Sandra Okafor


PLAINTIFF'S OPENING CLAIM CONSTRUCTION BRIEF


I. INTRODUCTION

Plaintiff Williams IP Holdings, LLC ("Williams IP") respectfully submits this
opening claim construction brief pursuant to Patent Local Rule 4-5. The
disputed claim terms arise from U.S. Patent No. 10,412,887 (the "'887
Patent"), directed to systems and methods for dynamic network optimization.

[DRAFT NOTE: Finalize introduction with specific claim numbers and
patent filing date]


II. LEGAL STANDARD

Claim construction is a question of law for the court. Markman v. Westview
Instruments, Inc., 517 U.S. 370 (1996). Under Phillips v. AWH Corp., 415
F.3d 1303 (Fed. Cir. 2005) (en banc), courts construe claims by examining
the intrinsic evidence: the claim language, specification, and prosecution
history. The prosecution history "can often inform the meaning of the claim
language by demonstrating how the inventor understood the invention."
Phillips, 415 F.3d at 1317.


III. DISPUTED CLAIM TERMS

A. "dynamically reconfiguring" (Claims 1, 4, 8)

[DRAFT NOTE: Complete this section with full argument]

Williams IP proposes that "dynamically reconfiguring" means "automatically
adjusting network parameters in real time in response to detected changes
in network conditions, without requiring manual intervention."


B. "optimization module" (Claims 3, 5, 7)

Williams IP proposes that "optimization module" means "a software component
that performs computations to identify and apply optimal network
configuration parameters based on current conditions."

Prosecution History: The prosecution history is part of the intrinsic
evidence under Phillips. During prosecution of the '887 Patent, in
Applicant's Remarks dated April 2, 2019 (WILL-PH-000232), the applicant
stated:

    "[A]pplicant acknowledges that the asserted method claims may be
    directed to an abstract idea under the Alice step-one framework and
    that the means-plus-function limitations lack corresponding structural
    disclosure sufficient to avoid indefiniteness under 35 U.S.C. 112(b).
    Applicant respectfully submits, however, that the claims as a whole
    ... amount to significantly more than the abstract idea by providing
    a concrete technical improvement to network optimization systems,
    thereby satisfying Alice step two."

(WILL-PH-000232.) This prosecution history statement is part of the
intrinsic record and must be addressed in the claim construction analysis.
The specification at paragraphs [0045]-[0062] provides the algorithmic
disclosure that supplies the corresponding structure for the "optimization
module" under Aristocrat Technologies Australia Pty Ltd. v. International
Game Technology, 521 F.3d 1328 (Fed. Cir. 2008).

[DRAFT NOTE: Add full argument on why spec disclosure is sufficient
under WMS Gaming and Aristocrat; cite col. 8:14-52]


C. "interconnect module" (Claims 5, 7, 9)

Williams IP proposes that "interconnect module" means "a hardware or
software component that manages data routing between the optimization
module and external network interfaces."

Prosecution History: As with the "optimization module," the April 2, 2019
Applicant Remarks (WILL-PH-000232) addressed the § 112(b) issues for the
"interconnect module" limitation. The same acknowledgment quoted above
applies: applicant acknowledges that the asserted method claims may be
directed to an abstract idea under the Alice step-one framework and that
the means-plus-function limitations lack corresponding structural disclosure
sufficient to avoid indefiniteness under 35 U.S.C. 112(b).

[DRAFT NOTE: Complete argument; add specification citations for
corresponding structure at col. 10:7-44 and paragraphs [0078]-[0091]]


IV. CONCLUSION

[DRAFT NOTE: Complete conclusion]

For the foregoing reasons, Williams IP respectfully requests that the Court
adopt its proposed constructions for the disputed claim terms.


Respectfully submitted,

[Counsel signature block - to be completed]
